title: Book 8 — Urania, Chapter 110
paragraphs: Themistocles, then, by speaking thus was trying to deceive them, and the Athenians followed his advice. For he had had the reputation even in former times of being an able man, and he had now proved himself truly both capable and of good judgment; so they were ready in every way to follow his counsel when he spoke. So, once these had been persuaded by him, Themistocles at once sent men in a boat — whom he trusted to keep silence no matter what test they might be put to — with what he charged them to tell the king; and among them was again Sikinnos his servant. When they came to Attica, the rest stayed behind in the ship while Sikinnos went up to Xerxes and spoke these words: “Themistocles son of Neocles has sent me — Themistocles who is commander of the Athenians and the best and ablest man of all the allies — to tell you that Themistocles the Athenian, wishing to do you a service, held back the Greeks when they wanted to pursue your ships and destroy the bridges on the Hellespont. You may, therefore, make your way home quite undisturbed.” Having delivered this, they sailed back.
